name: Stage Redundant Identity Cue Vocabulary 01
bounded_question: What minimal non-color shape or motif vocabulary can give 2–5 present Characters a stable redundant visual identity cue at the Stage floor/name hinge without encoding mutable state, psychology, role, Perspective, Opportunity or creator authority?
authority_limits: Human-readable Character names remain the primary explicit identity channel.
The cue is redundant visual identity support, not a replacement for stable programmatic identity or accessible naming.
CIR-S1 does not select a final icon family, app symbol, palette, typeface, motion system, Character psychology vocabulary or implementation token.
STA-01 focus/selection treatment remains separate; C0 Threshold K remains the provisional primary app-symbol incumbent and is not a Character cue source.
Three pips and inter-Character arcs remain outside scope and acquire no meaning here.
No result resolves ODR-05, ODR-07, ODR-14, ODR-15, ODR-19 or ODR-30.

reentry_law.prior_closure: CIR-T1R1 closed the earlier identity-mechanics visual laboratory and handed forward laws rather than a selected surface.
reentry_law.new_basis: Phase C plus PKT-STAGE-CORE-02 creates a later frozen incumbent whose Stage law explicitly requires a non-color redundant identity cue while leaving the exact visual vocabulary unresolved.

CNEG.name: Identical Ring Negative Control
CNEG.grammar: same simple ring for every Character
CNEG.expected_failure: cannot distinguish Characters after visible names recede

CINC.name: Incumbent Primitive Outline Control
CINC.grammar: simple familiar primitive outlines transcribing the incumbent placeholder class without claiming exact pixel identity

F1.name: Faceted Contour
F1.grammar: one compact closed asymmetric contour per Character; identity difference lives only in perimeter topology
F1.forbidden_drift: shield, gem, map pin, letterform, rank badge

F2.name: Broken Perimeter
F2.grammar: one compact open contour composed of two unequal perimeter segments with Character-specific gap relation
F2.forbidden_drift: progress ring, clock, loading state, gauge, activity status

F3.name: Offset Pair
F3.grammar: two unequal non-touching strokes or masses in a Character-specific asymmetrical relation
F3.forbidden_drift: pause, equals, link, people, quotation marks, transport/control glyph

F4.name: Aperture Field
F4.grammar: shared compact outer field with a Character-specific non-semantic interior aperture
F4.forbidden_drift: camera, eye, keyhole, letter counterform, badge or software-category icon

family_separation_law: F1 identity varies by outer silhouette only; F2 by open-perimeter gap relation; F3 by two-part relation; F4 by interior negative space.
No candidate may be a one-parameter mutation of another family.
No candidate may use current Character color, portrait, initials, names, occupation, biography, role, emotion, faction, rank, relationship strength or Stage state to construct its geometry.
Current incumbent floor symbols are evidence/control only and receive no automatic candidate status.
neutralization: cue visible paint is currentColor only
no gradients, glow, shadow, texture, animation or material identity
no letters, initials, numbers, portraits, faces or semantic pictograms
no Threshold K or wordmark geometry
cue geometry is identical across Rest, Listening, Selected, Current Opportunity and Speaking test states
state treatment is external to the cue and may not modify cue paths

matrix.rule: Within one family, each Character owns one immutable cue geometry reused across every layout, size, mode and state.

mechanical_floors: all cue SVGs are self-contained, deterministic and external-resource-free
visible cue paint uses currentColor only
five distinct cue definitions exist per promotable family
CNEG is intentionally identical and ineligible
every Character cue is reused unchanged in every state-collision cell
visual names may be reduced only in a labeled stress condition while an accessible Character name remains present
no cue contains text, aria-label duplication or interactive semantics
no horizontal overflow at 320 CSS px
12/16/20/24/32 px size strip preserves recognizable family topology without clipping
forced-colors compatibility cannot depend on authored color
pairwise differentiation within a family must survive monochrome and loss of Stage position
subjective_falsification_after_clean_pre: FAIL a family if two Character cues are readily confusable at 16–20 px when names are visually reduced.
FAIL if the cue reads primarily as mutable status, progress, selection, Opportunity, speaking, emotion, role, profession, faction or rank.
FAIL if the cue becomes a familiar software/category pictogram rather than neutral identity support.
FAIL if the cue visually overpowers the Character name or floor pool.
FAIL if a family requires color, motion, exact Stage position or surrounding cone geometry to distinguish its members.
FAIL if Selected/Opportunity/Speaking overlays make the identity cue appear to change identity.
FAIL if narrow/reduced conditions require a different cue geometry.
PASS means only that a cue family survives as a bounded Phase-C identity mechanism for Stage composition testing.

result_law.promotion_scope: provisional Stage redundant-identity cue mechanism only; no production token or final shared icon family

review_order: 2. 12/16/20 px pairwise differentiation and semantic-drift audit
5. name-visually-reduced recovery with accessible names retained
6. state-collision audit with immutable cue geometry
7. freeze Design Sol view before any Director taste input if more than one lawful survivor remains
explicit_non_authority: No full Stage successor render is authorized by this method freeze alone.
No final iconography system, palette, typeface, motion token, WinUI behavior, accessibility validation, Store asset or implementation is claimed.
Browser/static evidence cannot be relabeled as native Windows screen-reader, high-contrast, WACK or runtime validation.
